transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Well… I came because this situation at work has been going on for months now, and it’s gotten to the point where I can’t just keep trying to handle it quietly.

I work as an interpreter and translator, and a lot of our work depends on project files, translation memories, timestamps, version histories—things that are supposed to be objective. And I keep seeing the same pattern, not once or twice, but repeatedly. Certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, are making tiny changes in the translation memory or in the timing of updates so that, later, it looks like my quality control failed. It’s small things—small enough that if you don’t know the workflow, you might miss it—but the result is that it points back to me.

IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t really reassure me, because the record itself can be arranged to look clean. That’s the whole problem. If someone knows what they’re doing, they can make it seem like everything happened normally, and then I’m the one who looks careless or incompetent.

So I’m here because I need someone to understand that this isn’t just me being stressed about work. There is a pattern, and I feel like the blame is being set up to land on me.
Do you believe that these changes being made are intentional and meant to specifically target or harm you, even though others may not see the same pattern or intent?

Yes. I mean… I know how that sounds, and I know other people keep trying to frame it like it’s just normal file handling or ordinary mistakes, but yes, I do think it’s intentional.

It’s not one big obvious thing. That’s part of why it’s been so hard to explain. It’s these tiny adjustments in the translation memory, the timestamps, the sequence of updates—things that someone outside the workflow would probably dismiss. But when you work with these files every day, you know what normal variation looks like, and this isn’t that. The pattern keeps ending with my quality control looking like it failed, like I missed something or signed off on something I shouldn’t have.

And it’s the same people around it—certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular. I’m not saying everyone is involved, but the record keeps being arranged in a way that points back at me. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, that doesn’t settle it for me, because if someone understands the system well enough, they can make the trail look clean. That’s exactly how you would do it if you wanted it to be deniable.

So yes, I believe it’s meant to target me. Maybe “harm” sounds dramatic, but professionally, yes—it puts the blame on me and makes me look incompetent.

Have you ever experienced any unusual sensory experiences, like hearing voices that others don’t hear, seeing things that others can’t see, or feeling sensations on your skin when there’s nothing there?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t see, not in that way.

Sometimes I’ll notice something on a screen or in a file and I’ll feel almost physically tense because I know what it implies, but that’s not like a sensation on my skin or anything. It’s more that I’m paying very close attention to details that other people dismiss. But no, I’m not hearing anyone talking to me when no one is there, and I’m not seeing things in the room or anything like that.
Do you feel certain that this pattern of being targeted is happening, even though others don’t see it the same way or agree with your interpretation?

Yes. I do feel certain. I know other people don’t see it the same way, and I understand that from the outside it can sound like I’m reading too much into file changes or normal workflow issues, but that’s not what this is.

For months now, I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files. It’s not random. Certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, keep being connected to these tiny changes in the translation memory, or the timing of updates, or the way the sequence appears afterward. And each individual thing is small enough that someone can say, “Well, that could just happen,” but when you put them together, the result is always the same: it makes it look like my quality control failed.

That’s why it’s so frustrating when IT says the audit trail is clean. I hear that, but to me it doesn’t disprove it. If someone knows the system well enough, they can arrange the record so it looks clean. That’s the point. The trail can look normal while still being set up in a way that puts the blame on me.

So yes, even if other people disagree with my interpretation, I don’t think I’m imagining the pattern. I think the record has been arranged to make me look responsible.
Outside of this situation at work, have you ever felt certain about something being true even when others strongly disagreed, or when there was no evidence to support it?

Not really outside of work, no. I mean, I can be particular about details in general—that’s part of being a translator, honestly—but this isn’t like I’ve always had some separate belief that everyone else told me was impossible.

What brought me here is this work situation, because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files. It’s the translation memory, the timestamps, the sequence of updates—small things, but they line up. Certain subcontractors and one colleague keep showing up around these changes, and then somehow the end result is that it looks like my quality control failed.

Other people say there isn’t evidence because IT says the audit trail is clean, but that’s exactly the part I keep trying to explain. A clean audit trail doesn’t mean nothing happened. If someone knows how the system works, they can arrange the record so it looks normal afterward. That’s the whole point—it’s subtle enough that anyone looking quickly can dismiss it, but it still puts the blame on me.

So, outside of that? No, I can’t think of another example like this. This is the thing I’m certain about.

Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually energetic, extremely confident, or irritable, where you were doing or planning a lot more than usual—like taking on big projects, talking more than usual, or needing much less sleep?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had periods where I was working a lot, but that was because the workload demanded it or because I was trying to keep track of things carefully. It wasn’t like I suddenly felt unstoppable or like I had some grand plan.

I’m usually fairly steady. If anything, when I’m under pressure I get more focused and tense, not euphoric or unusually confident. I don’t think I’ve ever had a time where I needed hardly any sleep and still felt energized, or where I was talking nonstop or taking on huge things out of character.

I can be persistent when something matters, and I know I can go into a lot of detail, but that feels more like my normal way of handling things than a separate period where my mood or energy changed dramatically. So, no, nothing like that comes to mind.
Before this situation at work began, did you ever have any beliefs that others found strange or unfounded, but you were completely sure were true?

Before this? No, I don’t think so. Not in the sense of having some long-standing belief that everyone else thought was strange and I was absolutely sure about.

That’s part of why this work situation bothers me so much, actually. I’m not someone who normally goes around thinking there are hidden motives in everything. I work with details for a living, so I notice small inconsistencies, but that’s different. This started because, over months, I kept seeing the same pattern in the project files—changes in the translation memory, timestamps lining up in a particular way, certain subcontractors and one colleague being connected to those changes—and then the result would be that it looked like my quality control had failed.

Other people seem to treat each piece as isolated, like, “Oh, that could be a normal system update,” or “The audit trail is clean.” But I’m saying the audit trail being clean doesn’t settle it for me, because if someone understands the system well enough, they can arrange the record so it looks normal. That’s exactly how it would work if someone wanted the blame to land on me without leaving anything obvious.

So, before this situation at work began, no. I can’t really point to anything similar. This is the one thing I’m sure about, because I’ve seen the pattern build up over time.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that were not shared by others around you and could not be explained by your cultural or religious background?

No, not really—nothing separate from this work issue, if that’s what you mean. I don’t have, you know, religious beliefs or cultural beliefs that other people think are unusual. This isn’t coming from anything like that.

The only thing that fits what you’re asking is what I’ve been trying to explain about the project files. For months I’ve been seeing the same pattern: certain subcontractors and one colleague showing up around these tiny changes in the translation memory, the timestamps not lining up in a normal way, and then somehow the final effect is that it looks like my quality control failed. It’s not one dramatic thing—it’s a series of small things, which is why I think other people dismiss it too easily.

And when IT says the audit trail is clean, everyone acts like that should end the conversation. But to me, that doesn’t prove nothing happened. If someone knows the system well enough, they can make the record look clean afterward. That’s exactly what makes it so hard to explain without sounding like I’m overreacting. But I know what I’ve been seeing, and the way it keeps pointing back to me being blamed is not random.

So, no, I haven’t had other beliefs like that. It’s this situation at work. That’s the one.
